Relationship & Escalation Liaison

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

- Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant - Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

THE ROLE

Due to our rapid growth and the sensitivity of our proprietary materials discovery platform, we are seeking a Security Engineer to ensure our innovation happens at speed without compromising the safety of our IP or our users.

YOUR IMPACT

In this role you will be building the automated security pipelines and AI-specific guardrails that protect our frontier models and research data, which is critical for maintaining the integrity of our materials discovery engine and the trust of our global partners.

 

As an early security hire, you won't be a manual blocker; instead, you will architect a "shift-left" culture where security is a fundamental product feature. Your work ensures that as we scale our search for next-generation materials, our underlying infrastructure and world-class IP remain safely locked down.

AI-Specific Security & IP Protection

Cloud Security, CI/CD & Core DevSecOps

- Weave automated security “guardrails” directly into our CI/CD workflows, including secret scanning, API exposure checks, and software composition analysis (SCA).

- Codify security policies using Infrastructure as Code (IaC), ensuring all cloud resources are automatically compliant with global standards (e.g. GDPR, SOC2).

- Manage secrets and vulnerability patching for containerized environments (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes) to ensure our research environment is resilient.

- Design strict, least-privilege Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls to isolate sensitive training data and research workloads.

Interdisciplinary Collaboration & Security Culture

- Lead incident response efforts by monitoring production logs for anomalies and collaborating with AI Researchers to deploy rapid fixes.

- Empower the engineering team to own security by providing tools for local IDE security scanning and pre-commit hooks.

- Act as a security educator, cultivating a culture of shared responsibility across the AI, chemistry, and engineering teams.

- Partner with researchers, chemists, and engineers to translate security requirements into practical workflows that support rather than slow down scientific work.

MUST HAVE SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS:

- You are motivated by the mission of using AI for planetary-scale impact and understand the high stakes of securing "deep tech" intellectual property.

- 3+ years of experience in a DevSecOps, Cloud Security, or Site Reliability Engineering role, preferably within a fast-paced startup or AI-centric company.

- Proven experience building and securing CI/CD pipelines (e.g. GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins).

- Strong proficiency

title: Trusted Access Operations Lead
description:
About the team

Trusted Access helps eligible customers access and use advanced AI capabilities with appropriate safeguards. Within User Safety & Risk Operations, we connect customer onboarding, eligibility review, access provisioning, and support into a service customers can navigate with confidence.

We work with Product, Engineering, technical support, regional operations, and customer-facing teams to resolve difficult access problems and improve the systems behind them. Our work combines sound judgment on individual cases with better products, clearer guidance, and automation that reduces unnecessary friction.

About the role

We’re looking for a senior operations leader to own the Trusted Access operating strategy and lead a team of risk-operations specialists. You will set priorities across programs, build a reliable customer access service, and hire, manage, and develop your direct reports.

This role combines program ownership with formal people management. You will establish shared commitments with technical support and regional escalation leaders, who manage their own teams, and bring those groups together around customer outcomes. You’ll stay close enough to complex cases to challenge assumptions while giving specialists the ownership and capacity to fix recurring problems.

Success means customers reach the right access outcome with clear communication, teams make consistent decisions, and the service scales with less avoidable escalation and manual work.

In this role, you will:

- Own the operating strategy and roadmap across Trusted Access programs, translating customer needs and organizational priorities into clear service commitments, ownership, and investment decisions.

- Build a coherent customer journey from application and eligibility review through approval, provisioning coordination, and confirmed access, including appeals and subsequent access changes. Establish clear handoffs and route exceptions to authorized decision-makers.

- Hire, coach, and develop your team. Set expectations, delegate meaningful ownership, give direct feedback, address performance gaps, and build the capabilities needed as programs grow.

- Make capacity and prioritization decisions across urgent customer needs, launch readiness, and lasting improvements. Coordinate regional coverage, vendor support, and backup with partner teams while protecting time to eliminate recurring work.

- Lead consequential customer escalations, bringing incomplete or conflicting evidence into a clear decision process. Align owners on the next action and ensure customers receive accurate updates and a clear resolution.

- Turn support patterns into a prioritized roadmap with Product and Engineering: improve onboarding, provisioning workflows, tooling, self-service, and AI-assisted operations. Validate that changes work before expanding them.

- Establish measures of service health and decision quality. Distinguish fast responses from actual resolution, investigate persistent delays, and use evidence to change priorities.

- Prepare new programs and customer channels for launch and scale. Align support responsibilities, review standards, customer guidance, and technical dependencies; make readiness gaps and tradeoffs clear to leadership.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have built and run complex customer support, onboarding, access, risk, or service operations, with measurable improvements beyond handling more volume.

- Have formally managed people through hiring, development, difficult feedback, and performance decisions, and can show how your leadership increased the team’s capability and ownership. 5+ years of management experience preferred.

- Can make defensible tradeoffs among customer commitments, safeguards, service quality, and capacity, even when stakeholders disagree or the evidence is incomplete.

- Have led work across teams you do not manage, resolving ownership gaps and negotiating commitments that hold up in execution.

title: Product Director, Professional Services
description:
The Role
Unit4 serves a global community of professional services organizations - management consultancies, engineering and architectural practices, IT services firms, audit and advisory, and legal services. These businesses run on people: utilization, engagement profitability, and project delivery define how they win or lose. As Product Director for Professional Services, you own the vertical product vision, strategy, and roadmap that makes Unit4 the ERP of choice for mid-market PSOs.
This is not a generalist PM role with an industry overlay. You will have dedicated engineering capacity to build genuine vertical depth in the platform - industry-specific capabilities that horizontal product teams cannot and will not build. You will work in close partnership with horizontal PMs across Financials, HR, Projects, and Procurement to ensure the full platform delivers for PSOs end-to-end. You own the backlog, the outcomes, the roadmap, and the commercial case for why your vertical wins.
AI is actively reshaping how professional services firms operate. The automation of billable work, the compression of traditional T&M models, and the shift toward outcome- and subscription-based pricing are rewriting the economics of the sector. The right candidate understands where these firms are in that journey and what it means for the software they need. You have built enterprise software for PSOs, you know what the best solutions in this space do well and where they fall short, and you can translate an industry in transition into a product roadmap that stays ahead of it.
What You'll Do

• Own the Professional Services product vision, strategy, and multi-horizon roadmap; align it with Unit4 's platform strategy and commercial growth targets.

• Own feature outcomes, not just delivery - define clear adoption, usage, and customer impact goals for every capability you champion, and track performance against them after launch.

• Serve as the internal authority on the Professional Services vertical, providing product, marketing, analyst relations, and pre-sales teams with the industry grounding they need to position, demonstrate, and sell effectively.

• Lead a prioritized product backlog with dedicated engineering capacity - defining outcomes, success metrics, release plans, and quality criteria.

• Translate deep PSO market knowledge into specific, investment-backed product requirements: opportunity sizing, problem statements, and build-vs-partner decisions.

• Define industry-specific solution blueprints, reference configurations, and pre-built templates that accelerate customer time-to-value.

• Act as the vertical voice in planning conversations with horizontal product teams, ensuring PSO requirements are reflected in platform investment.

• Partner with the Industry Growth Director on launch readiness, pricing, packaging, and field enablement for new capabilities.

• Engage directly with strategic customers and the PS Industry Board to validate roadmap direction, co-innovate, and generate outcome evidence.

• Monitor the competitive landscape - know what NetSuite, Workday, Deltek, Kantata, and others are shipping and what it means for Unit4 's positioning.

• Work with partners to extend the value proposition for PSO customers.

title: Executive & Personal Assistant to the CEO (Hybrid)
description:
About Hone

Hone is an online medical clinic at the forefront of transforming healthcare and enhancing longevity. We use cutting-edge scientific advancements to empower men and women to take control of their health and unlock their full potential. Our people are the heart of everything we do and drive our success. We approach every project through our brand values:

• Fight for the Customer

• Execute Ruthlessly

• Communicate Candidly, Clearly, and Kindly

• Collaborate Selflessly

• Practice Calculated Risk-Taking

• Maximize Joy and Gratitude

Hone has been fully virtual from day one and will continue to be a remote-first employer.

Our Ideal Candidate

Our ideal candidate is a mission-driven, motivated multi-tasker who is invested in work that is fulfilling and impactful. They embrace change and tackle challenges with enthusiasm. They have an “all-in” disposition towards work, understanding that we are a fast-paced, high-growth organization with evolving priorities. They can excel at both independent tasks and collaborative work, leading with clear and candid communication. They exhibit humble leadership-the ability to drive initiatives forward while remaining excited about continuous learning and development opportunities. They feel strongly about being part of a team that advocates for people to live longer and better lives.

The Role

You will give our CEO hours back every week. You will run his inbox and calendar, own his follow-ups, and take recurring personal and logistical tasks off his plate. This is a hybrid executive assistant and personal assistant role, starting at roughly 15 hours a week and will flex up based on success, with regular in-person time in Jersey City.

What you'll do

• Manage the CEO's email and calendar through delegate access. Learn his preferences and know what to escalate to him.

• Keep one shared tracker of what teams are waiting on from him, and send materials so nothing stalls.

• Run the Friday speaker program: source speakers, run prep calls, send the honorarium, and schedule sessions.

• Schedule internal meetings, prepare briefs, and follow up with owners on action items.

• Handle recurring personal upkeep items and shipping business-related materials.

• Take on miscellaneous requests as they come up, and document anything repeatable so it runs without prompting.

• Coordinate recurring touchpoints with partner teams as assigned.

What we're looking for

• Several years supporting a founder or senior executive. You already know how to run someone's email and calendar.

• Comfort with hands-on personal tasks and no ego about them.

• Proactive and fast. You respond quickly and close loops without being chased.

• Sound judgment and discretion with confidential business and personal information.

• Based in or near Jersey City and able to work in-person regularly.

• Fluent in Google Workspace and Slack. Experience with Asana and AI tools is a plus.

What success looks like

• The CEO's calendar and inbox run without him thinking about them.

• Personal tasks no longer pile up or interrupt his workday.

• Every team request that is waiting on him is visible, tracked, and moving.

Logistics

• Hours: roughly 15 per week to start (a mix of in-person and remote).

• Reports directly to the CEO.

• Employment type: Independent Contractor (1099) to start will the potential to convert to full-time (including salary/benefits) based on performance.

• Compensation: Hourly, flexible based on experience.

• Start date: As soon as possible.

Benefits*

Hone wants our team to be in the best condition of their lives, so we offer a range of benefits including:

• A remote-first work environment

• Competitive compensation and equity options

• Health, dental, and vision insurance coverage

• Short-term disability and basic life coverage

• Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs)

• Lifestyle Spending Accounts (LSAs)

• We follow federal holidays and have uncapped time off for exempt employees

• Budget

title: Forecasting Expert
description:
About the opportunity:

As a Forecasting Analyst in the WFM team, you are responsible for producing high quality demand forecasts for different workstreams across operations. Your forecasts will be used for capacity planning, budget planning, and shift scheduling of our in-house teams and external partners. Additionally your forecasting expertise will be used to support the implementation of new products and key initiatives, and you will be the internal go-to person for forecasting related questions. You will challenge existing frameworks and implement innovative solutions using your experience and knowledge.

 

In this role, you will:

•
Forecast resource requirements across different teams and workstreams to meet customer/stakeholder demand and required service levels.

•
Produce analytics on forecast performance, as well as volume evolution and the effect of internal or external factors on volume such as new product launches.

•
Assist in the further development of forecasting methodologies, models and tools in order to increase forecast accuracy and efficiency.

•
Partner with Growth, Membership, and Product Teams to understand the key drivers of volume and incorporate them into the forecasting and planning process.

•
Provide consultative support for the leadership team, guiding and advising to develop effective productivity measures, performance management intelligence and resource planning effectiveness.

•
Collaborate with a broad range of analytics teams at N26 to utilise shared platforms, insights and innovations.

•
Maintain an accurate events log detailing what is included in the forecast and reasons for variance to forecast.

 

What you need to be successful:

•
2+ years of experience working in demand forecasting, resource planning, or directly related field

•
Advanced level of ability in applied mathematics, statistics, scenario modelling, demand modelling and analysis

•
Expert with Excel or Google Sheets, and ability with SQL, Python, or R is a huge plus

•
Experience with business analytics platforms such as Google Looker, Metabase, or similar systems

•
Graduated with a degree in Statistics, Mathematics, or other related field of study/relevant level of professional experience

 

Traits:

•
Actively help yourself (and others) be successful.

•
Continuously learn and challenge the status quo.

•
Think globally, act locally.

•
Strong bias for action.

•
Give and receive open, direct and timely feedback.

title: Sr. Software Engineer - IT Software Engineering
description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale - unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data - securing and protecting private information more effectively - Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

Could we build a better version of an expensive SaaS tool on Elasticsearch? Our new IT Software Engineering team asks that question about the software Elastic pays for, and then we build the answer. Each system helps run the company day to day and becomes a reference architecture for Elastic's own products.

We're a team of builders, and this is a hands-on, 100% individual contributor role. Every engineer here owns their work end to end: shaping the problem, designing the system, shipping it, and keeping it healthy for years. Knowing what to build, and what not to build, matters more here than typing speed.

What this role is not: 

• Not a front-end role. The user interface follows a shared kit and is the simplest part of the work.

• Not a prototype or demo role. What we ship runs in production and is maintained for years.

• Not vibe coding. We use AI to build faster, not to skip design, review or testing.

• Not SaaS administration or configuration , and not an infrastructure-only or DevOps-only role.

• Not a people-management role.

What You Will Be Doing

• Take an open business problem, decide what to build and what to leave out, and turn it into a clear spec, data model and API contracts.

• Build internal applications that replace paid, specialized tools.

• Solve the hard parts that all of these applications share:

• reading data from several systems of record accurately and efficiently, without overloading or slowing those systems down

• storing sensitive data so it never leaks

• enforcing permissions on the server, so each person sees only the records and fields they are allowed to see

• Design and evolve the shared, versioned building blocks that every application is built from: data connectors, authorization, data storage and migrations, search, and reporting.

• Build with AI coding agents such as Claude Code inside a disciplined, spec-driven process. Acceptance criteria are traced to tests, interface contracts get compatibility checks, and small slices are reviewed and proven before the next one starts. Automated quality gates decide when work is done.

• Own what you build for its whole life: review, testing, releases, production operations including on-call, new features, maintenance and, eventually, retirement.

• Help set the team's standards for architecture, contracts, testing and observability, and feed what you learn back into Elastic's products.

What You Bring 

• Senior-level experience designing, shipping and maintaining production backend systems through failures and changing requirements, not just launching them.

• Sound judgment about what to build, what to leave out, and how to keep a system simple as its requirements change. You apply abstraction, separation of concerns, single responsibility, SOLID and common design patterns where they fit.

• Strong API and data design: clear contracts and careful data models, and the ability to change both without breaking the people who depend on them.

• Experience integrating with other systems (APIs, databases, event streams) safely and efficiently.

• Security-first thinking about authorization and sensitive data.

• Search fundamentals. You can explain:

• how information is indexed and how text is processed

• how results are scored and ranked

• when to use keyword, vector (semantic) or hybrid se

title: Fleet Partnerships Lead
description:
ABOUT US

Quartermaster is building the most comprehensive real-time picture of activity on the world's oceans. We do it by placing next-generation sensing equipment aboard commercial ships and turning the global fleet itself into a living network that illuminates the maritime domain in ways legacy AIS never could. Better maritime domain awareness means safer mariners, more secure sea lanes, and an ocean that can no longer go dark. Every vessel we bring onto the network extends that picture a little further.

The network only exists if ships join it. This role owns that mission end-to-end: enlisting the right vessels across priority ship types and regions. You will find target fleets, win over owners, close agreements, and shepherd the relationships that keep them contributing to the network long term.

This role sits at the foundation of how we scale. Rather than stepping into a rigid playbook, you will actively participate in designing and refining our acquisition workflow from day one. You’ll work with the team to evolve our early outreach into an efficient, repeatable engine that brings hundreds and thousands of vessels onto the network.

WHAT YOU'LL BUILD:

- Engineer vessel recruitment from initial discovery to qualification, contract close, and long-term retention into a repeatable, data-driven operational funnel.

- Synchronize supply acquisition with Quartermaster’s broader growth targets and regional maritime coverage demands so deployment teams are never bottlenecked by vessel availability.

- Determine headcount needs by ship type, geography, and stage of acquisition; hire, mentor, and level up acquisition specialists and field leads as the company expands.

- Cultivate deep subject matter expertise across key maritime segments (e.g., container, bulk, tankers, specialized craft) within the team to eliminate coverage blind spots.

- Lead from the front by closing high-priority partner fleets yourself, while developing standard operating procedures and training your team to hit sustained targets.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Target & Close High-Value Fleets: Work from prioritized lists of critical vessel types, initiate direct outreach to shipowners, operators, and technical managers, and close commercial partnerships.

- Own Partner Relationships: Serve as a trusted advisor to maritime executives, technical managers, and port agents globally to ensure high alignment and fast contract turnaround.

- Maintain Buffer Capacity: Keep a healthy surplus of qualified, signed vessels in reserve across key maritime hubs so installation teams can deploy without idle time.

- Operationalize the Funnel: Instrument acquisition metrics, tracking pipeline health, stage velocity, conversion rates, and acquisition costs.

OUTCOMES YOU'LL OWN

- Fleet Coverage Velocity: Deliver qualified vessels to the network on schedule to meet regional and global coverage mandates.

- Supply Unit Economics: Manage incentives, connectivity arrangements, and field support costs to preserve network margin.

- Network Quality: Prioritize mission-critical, high-impact vessel classes over low-utility volume.

- Operational Repeatability: Establish a documented, hardened acquisition playbook that new team members can run out of the box.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 4-7+ years of relevant experience: Demonstrated track record in supply acquisition, operations management, marketplace expansion, or business development-with direct ownership of supply-side rollouts, partner recruitment, or field-based acquisition.

- Proven 0-to-1 builder: Hands-on experience entering new markets, regions, or segments with no established playbook, standing up supply networks from scratch, and leaving behind repeatable processes that others can execute.

- Funnel architecture & discipline: Skilled at transforming unstructured, relationship-driven deal-making into a structured, trackable acquisition engine powered by clear milestones, pipeline hygiene, and operational rigor.

- Team leadership

title: Data Center Architect
description:
Role Profile

Job Title: Data Centre Architect

Reports to: Head of Data Centre Development

Location: UK hybrid

Company Overview:

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure - from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we’re building this organisation from the ground up. We’re looking for people who’d rather build the playbook than inherit one - who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of team you’ve previously managed.

This is a senior individual contributor role with authority to sign off technical schedules, working with cluster and network architects, NVIDIA and other OEM engineers, colocation provider engineering and sales teams, and the internal Procurement, Legal, Finance and Site Operations teams.

What You’ll Do

You will be the single technical authority between our GPU-as-a-service business and the colocation providers that host our NVIDIA clusters. You turn cluster architecture and OEM requirements into a precise, contractable statement of work (SOW) for the data centre white space, then hold the provider to it through design, installation and acceptance.

We are growing from tens of megawatts to hundreds, on rack-scale liquid-cooled platforms at 130 kW per rack and rising to 200 kW and beyond. Mistakes in power, cooling or fibre specification show up as stranded capacity, delayed cluster delivery and disputes, so the role carries real commercial weight.

Key Responsibilities

Technical negotiation with colocation providers

- Lead technical due diligence on candidate sites: power availability and energisation dates, redundancy topology, liquid-cooling capability, floor loading, rack logistics, fibre and meet-me access.

- Negotiate the technical schedules of the colocation agreement with commercial and legal: capacity and density commitments, power and cooling SLAs, temperature and flow envelopes, metering, expansion rights, change control and remedies.

- Challenge provider claims with evidence: single-line diagrams, P&IDs, load-bank and commissioning records, reference customers.

Specification & SOW

- Work with cluster architects and OEMs (NVIDIA first) to capture rack, power, cooling, network and layout requirements, and keep them current across product generations.

- Write and own the technical SOW for white-space fitout: containment and cooling interfaces, power distribution to rack, structured cabling and pathways, rack and POD layout, security zoning, labelling and records.

- Define clear scope boundaries and responsibilities between us, the colocation provider, OEMs and installation contractors, with no gaps and no overlaps.

- Maintain a requirements baseline with traceability from OEM document, to SOW clause, to acceptance test.

Design, installation & acceptance

- Review provider and contractor designs, shop drawings and method statements against the SOW; run design reviews and close findings.

- Define acceptance: factory and site tests, liquid flush and cleanliness, power quality, thermal performance at full load, fibre loss, burn-in, and the evidence pack needed for each gate.

- Attend key witness tests and sign off, or reject, completion of each phase before hardware is energised.

- Manage technical change requests and variations, and advise on cost and schedule impact.

Knowledge & standards

- Build reusable reference designs, SOW templates and a site-scoring framework so each new deployment starts from a proven baseline.

- Track the roadmap

title: Senior Operations Account Manager - Mandarin Speaking , London
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

THE OPPORTUNITY

Some of our biggest accounts are Chinese platforms, 3PLs and brokers moving millions of parcels into the UK. They grow with us when parcels arrive on time, issues get fixed fast, and someone on our side always knows exactly what’s going on. That someone is you.

As our Mandarin-speaking Senior Operations Account Manager, you’ll take on some of the most complex of these accounts and set the standard for how we run account operations as we scale. Your mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure operations are never the reason a client hesitates to grow.

WHY THIS ROLE

A team behind every client. We’ve rebuilt our growth engine around small pods of three, built to win together. A Growth Lead owns the commercial relationship, a Program Manager triages internally to get initiatives over the line, and you own the operation that makes every promise real. Same clients, same goals, same numbers. No one carries a client alone, and every win is shared.

A real say in profitability. Margin is owned jointly by the pod through different lenses. When you cut parcel losses or make a collection run more efficiently, you’ll see exactly what it’s worth, and so will everyone else.

Scale that keeps moving. We plan to more than double daily volume by July 2027 and open one or two international markets. Your accounts, and your role, grow with that.

A career you can shape. Our Account Management team is tripling. Go deeper, taking on bigger and more complex accounts until you’re the expert the business leans on. Or go wider, across more pods, and in time lead others doing what you do.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Be the client’s go-to. Run the day-to-day relationship in Mandarin and English, on every channel, WeChat included.

- Own performance end to end. Know every metric that matters to your clients inside out, from on-time delivery to lost and undelivered parcels, and what’s driving each one. Then own every escalation from first report to final fix.

- Set the weekly rhythm. Lead weekly business reviews so clients hear the news from you first, good or bad.

- Make the forecast real. You won’t take a client’s forecast at face value. You’ll challenge it, sharpen it, and become the person whose numbers the network plans around.

- Protect the margin. Spot when an account’s profitability starts to slip, find the leak, and bring the recovery plan before anyone asks.

- Fix things once. Turn recurring issues into permanent fixes with our operations, quality and finance teams, then share them across every pod.

WHO WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE?

- You’re the person others call when a problem gets complicated, and you like it that way.

- You’ve led operational improvements that went beyond a single account, and you can show what they were worth.

- You can run a fix across operations, quality and finance at once: you map the dependencies, manage the risk and bring people with you.

title: Lab IT/OT Systems Administrator
description:
Your Impact at LILA

The Lab IT/OT Systems Administrator is a hands-on technology role responsible for the day-to-day administration, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of computing infrastructure inside Lila Sciences' laboratory environments. This role owns the layer of technology that sits between corporate IT and operational technology (OT), the workstations, edge compute, lab-area networking, and instrument-adjacent systems that enable autonomous science to run reliably.

Reporting to the Senior Director, OT Security and IT/OT Convergence, the Lab IT/OT Systems Administrator works in close partnership with the OT network architecture team, corporate IT operations, facilities/building automation, and laboratory operations leadership. The successful candidate is comfortable operating in a complex, fast-moving research environment where standard corporate IT practices do not always apply, where change control matters more than speed, and where the end users are scientists running irreplaceable experiments on highly specialized equipment.

This role is a key part of Lila's IT/OT convergence program. In addition to delivering day-to-day operational support, the person hired will contribute to the standards, device catalog, and playbooks that scale the function as the company grows, working under the direction of the Senior Director, OT Security and IT/OT Convergence.

What You'll Be Building

Lab IT Operations and Support

• Provide day-to-day administration and troubleshooting for laboratory computing assets, including lab-area workstations, edge compute nodes, lab-supplied PCs, and dedicated lab-network infrastructure (switches, access points, cabling).

• Respond to and resolve Lab IT incidents and service requests through the enterprise ITSM platform, applying appropriate prioritization for experiments in progress and time-sensitive scientific work.

• Maintain a strong on-site presence across Lila's laboratory locations; observe how scientists and lab operators use technology in practice and proactively identify issues before they become tickets.

• Coordinate scheduled maintenance windows for Lab IT systems in alignment with laboratory operations leadership; ensure changes do not disrupt active experiments.

Instrument-Adjacent and OT Boundary Support

• Provide IT-side support for laboratory instruments and automated platforms, including networking, identity integration, agent deployment decisions, and image/configuration alignment with company standards.

• Partner with the OT network architecture team, instrument vendors, and laboratory automation engineers to support new instrument deployments and changes, recognizing that instrument-connected systems require specialized handling distinct from standard corporate endpoints.

• Troubleshoot authentication, networking, and connectivity issues on vendor-supplied lab equipment, including systems with non-standard configurations, embedded operating systems, or unique vendor account models.

Asset Management and Inventory

• Maintain accurate, current Lab IT asset records in the enterprise CMDB, including device tier, owner, location, configuration baseline, and lifecycle state.

• Apply company labeling standards (QR/barcode asset tags linked to CMDB records) to Lab IT assets and conduct periodic ownership reconciliation.

• Serve as a primary point of contact when security or vulnerability management tools generate alerts on Lab IT assets, executing the workflow of alert review, asset identification, owner notification, and resolution.

Standards, Onboarding, and Procurement Support

• Contribute to the development and ongoing maintenance of the standardized device catalog and golden image program for laboratory computing equipment.

• Support the secure onboarding of new laboratory instruments and platforms, including baseline configuration, segmentation placement, monitoring enrollment, and owner assignment.
